newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian UES plans debt issue this year.
newsitem.headline: Russian UES plans debt issue this year.

text.p: Russian national electricity utility Unified Energy System (UES) is planning a debt issue this year but does not plan to issue shares, economy department chief Sergei Obratsov said on Wednesday.
He said regional utilities had not shown interest in issuing new shares, although they were able to do so.

"I do not know if it will be a Eurobond or not, but we plan to issue debt this year," Obratsov said in an interview. Interfax news agency on Tuesday quoted the government as recommending UES issue long-term debt this year.
"When and how much -- it is too early to say," Obratsov said.
He said RAO Yedinaya Energeticheskaya Sistema Rossii (UES) was not planning to issue new shares, which he said were dilutive, expensive and required the company to work to satisfy shareholders.
"If a normally functioning company launches an issue, then it is not working normally -- debt, yes," he said.
First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov on Tuesday said regional power utilities, most of which are controlled by UES, should raise new capital through share issues to fund restructuring.
Nemtsov is in charge of restructuring natural monopolies, huge companies without direct competitors such as UES. Others are gas company Gazprom, oil pipeline Transneft and the railways.
